newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile Enami union leader rules out strike.
newsitem.headline: Chile Enami union leader rules out strike.

text.p: Workers at Empresa Nacional de Mineria's copper smelter and refinery at Ventanas have ruled out the possibility of a strike when their pay contract ends on Friday, a union leader said.

Union president Luis Guerra said the workers' negotiating committee has accepted the basic terms of a new pay contract from Enami which means under Chilean law the workers no longer have the option to carry out a legal strike.
The union has been negotiating the fine print of the contract in recent weeks and workers will vote on two alternative deals in a secret ballot Tuesday, he said.
"The vote is between alternative contracts. The possibility of voting to strike does not exist," he told Reuters by telephone from Ventanas.
Both contracts are for five years, include a similar pay offer, but differ in benefits offered for long service, he said.

Negotiations at Ventanas have been different than those at Enami's Paipote smelter and state copper giant Codelco's Chuquicamata and Salvador pits, where workers had the option to reject a pay offer and go on strike.
Ventanas, which lies near Vina del Mar, refines 330,000 tonnes of copper a year.
